runs.content: Lockheed Martin picked up at the previous close ($536.15) — entered on a same-day UBS upgrade to Buy (PT $674 from $581, missile-segment revenue +150% 2025-2030) tied directly to fresh Iran/Saudi Arabia strikes pushing oil toward 3-month highs and a broad risk-off tape (Dow −600pts). TRV was exited discretionarily (−7.95%, −$79) to keep the book at 35 open positions after LMT's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions; AMGN fell −9.0% intraday on a Novartis Lp(a) trial-failure read-through (sector-wide biotech selling) but stayed net positive and was held. BR is now the weakest continuing position at −7.90%, no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,055 (+3.60% on $57,000).

US markets (NYSE/NASDAQ) were closed for Labor Day, so no new trade was entered. All 35 open positions were repriced off Friday Sept 4's close: no stop-losses, T1/T2 triggers, or signal exits fired, and no discretionary action was warranted — the healthiest cross-section of the book in recent runs, with zero positions at or below the −10% watch threshold. AVGO (Burry Sector Warning) remains the weakest continuing position at −7.21%, improved from −7.41%. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,577 (+4.60% on $56,000). Strategy selection and the weekly performance review resume Tuesday Sept 8.
